objective: Add a time synchronisation service to the rootfs topology, a clock plausibility check that refuses an unverified wall timestamp, a recorded reference offset for the bring-up step, and the statement that a container cannot repair a wrong host clock.
decision_supported: Can a wall-stamped evidence record be written from a clock nobody verified, and would the repository notice?
acceptance: robot-time-sync is added to services.yaml with its ordering, restart policy and safety_authority: false, plus a unit template, and the validator fails when the YAML and the unit set disagree.
A boot-time check refuses a wall timestamp earlier than the build date, and one whose implied boot time is earlier than the build date, reporting the discrepancy rather than stamping the record.
A reference-offset check records clock_offset_seconds beside the timestamp_utc and raw_capture_hash the bring-up plan already requires.
The container deployment documentation states that a container inherits the host clock and cannot repair a wrong host time, and gives the three reasons there is no container-side fix.
The evidence logger is ordered after robot-time-sync, and the ordering test proves that a unit ordered earlier fails validation.
observed_at is not reinterpreted and no new clock id is added.
evidence: validate_manifests.py: PASS, with robot-time-sync in the topology.
pytest tests/hardware/test_service_topology.py: 38 passed, with robot-time-sync added to the named exemption set and asserted safety_authority: false.
The failure paths: disabling both clock comparisons fails three tests; removing robot-time-sync from the logger After= line fails the validator with the service named.
make docs and check_doc_references.py: PASS, 182 pages.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: The change would require reinterpreting observed_at or adding a clock id; that is a contract question for the world model owner.
A container-side time fix would have to be added; the page explains why it would hide the problem rather than fix it.
A boot would have to be performed to claim the ordering works on a device; no device is available and the evidence is container and static.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to bsp/validation/bringup-plan.yaml or to the contracts.
data_classification: Repository-local YAML, systemd unit template, Python and Markdown. No credentials, private data or unreviewed assets.
model_policy: Deterministic Python, pytest and systemd-analyze; no model inference and no network access added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: A clock refusal could be read as discarding a record. It is not: the record stays, only the timestamp is marked unusable, and the check names which condition failed so the record is still usable for what it supports.

The tolerance is one second, which is a judgement. It is a named constant with its reason, and the bring-up step records the measured offset so a tighter or looser bound is a data question rather than a guess.

robot-time-sync is exempt from ordering after the safety monitor. It opens no bus and sets only the clock, and the exemption is a named set asserted to be safety_authority: false, so a fifth cannot be added quietly.
Rollback is a revert of this commit: the service and the clock check disappear and the logger returns to ordering after local-fs only. Nothing reads the check yet.
